title: 'Mirzapur' holds up a mirror to society—but is violence getting normalized in India?
description: In the film 'Mirzapur,' violence is a spectacle. The same can be said of a viral video of a woman biker attacked on a Gurugram street. The link between what a society watches and how it behaves is complex, but routine spectacles of brutality, especially against women, mustn’t normalize it.

title: President of Türkiye: No country should have the power to obstruct the will of the international community’s majority
description: The United Nations Security Council still reflects the structure of the post-World War II era. Reforms are needed to ensure a more effective, equitable and accountable approach to representation. Ending the veto privilege held by the UN’s big five could be a start.

title: Help India’s informal sector thrive: it supports mass livelihoods and has its own institutions of trust
description: The informal sector's interests matter. It accounts for nearly 90% of India’s workforce but functions on trust, reputation and relationships—its very own institutions. Indian policy, bent on formalization, must aim to strengthen and not replace this sector.

title: How RBI's rules for gadget loan recovery can make a positive difference for India on many counts
description: The Reserve Bank of India’s new rules that enable the use of technology tools to ensure loans for smartphones and other devices are duly repaid could drive up demand for these items. The idea can boost economic inclusion by taking gadget credit far and wide.

title: Himalayan glacial instability may be getting worse and that can alter the viability of dam projects
description: The Nepal catastrophe and others underscore why hydropower project finances must properly account for fast changing climate-related risks. India’s hydro plans that aim to maximize generation capacity must adjust to growing risk complexity.

title: The Tata case isn’t alone: why Jamie Dimon’s competition complaint can’t be taken lightly
description: JP Morgan’s chairman has expressed disappointment with the scenario of competition in India even as l’affaire Tata rages and global investors tune into Indian signals of governance. India’s economy can’t afford policy dissonance.

title: Mint Quick Edit | India’s economy has held up against global headwinds quite impressively
description: The country's growth outlook has brightened, as noted by credit rating agencies like Fitch, S&amp;P and Moody's. If India lives up to their raised GDP projections, it will testify to the tenacity of its economy.

title: AI doomsaying: Why much of what’s being said about AI power is best taken with a pinch of salt
description: By highlighting the risks of their own products, are AI leaders indulging in meta talk? As Big AI seeks public funds, they have an interest in drawing attention to the power of their technology. Since human nature prioritizes bad news over good, the industry has us listening.

title: American media is setting an example by circling wagons against Trump’s punitive moves
description: By filing a lawsuit against the Trump administration after the US President banned CNN, MS Now and Politico from the White House, the US press is resisting attempts to muzzle independent reporting. This is a lesson on the power of solidarity.

title: Customs duty: India must reform its default payment process to minimize logistical delays
description: The country's customs regime must trust importers to collect cargo first and pay duty later as a default rule. Don’t hold shipments hostage—it slows business operations, constrains exports and makes it harder for India to join global value chains.

title: There may be a case to rebalance climate spending but the energy transition must go on
description: For developing economies, money going into a clean-energy transition may be better spent elsewhere—such as health and education—as some experts argue. But that doesn’t diminish the urgency of climate action.

title: Investment research: ‘Buy’ and ‘sell’ are clear but what’s the point of the 'hold' rating awarded to stocks?
description: It owes its existence to an 'endowment bias' that makes people place an irrational price premium on what they own. Investors get even more attached to their investments than households objects. But smart investing means overcoming irrationality.

title: Why a unified compliance stack could unlock India’s startup potential
description: We have world-class founders, exceptional tech talent, and digital public infrastructure like UPI that have set global benchmarks. The next opportunity is to apply this exact infrastructure mindset to entrepreneurship itself.&nbsp;

title: Pax globalana: why India’s call for United Nations reform matters for global peace and prosperity
description: India’s demand for a better balanced UN Security Council assumes urgency in a world fraught with wars and tensions that multilateralism was meant to resolve. Other countries can trust India to help ensure that maps are never redrawn in blood.

title: Mint Quick Edit | The finance minister's call to imagine and not just make in India mustn’t fall on deaf ears
description: It’s true that India Inc must go beyond ‘Make in India' to ‘Imagine in India’ for the rest of the world. Innovation is what’s needed—not just for our economy to maximize its share of global value generation, but to make faster and broader progress.

title: When regulatory logic outruns its purpose
description: The RBI’s listing mandate for upper-layer NBFCs is rooted in transparency and market discipline. But applying the same logic to debt-free core investment companies raises questions about whether mandatory disclosure serves a clear public interest.

title: Agentic AI can be given access to digital public infrastructure only after they pass a security check
description: The OpenAI-Hugging Face scare over rogue agents rang a global alarm over how AI agents deployed in the real world may behave. As we start giving AI bots access to India’s digital stack of Aadhaar, UPI, etc, we’ll need strict protocols to keep out hostile agents.

title: Look this gift horse in the mouth: Newly married Trump Jr's wedding bash has raised a funding controversy
description: A party for the US President’s son fails a sniff test of how it was funded. Much of it was paid for by Umar Kremlev, an ally of Russian president Vladimir Putin. Eyebrows have got arched in America for obvious reasons.

title: Microsoft AI CEO: Anthropic’s AI constitution might sound advanced but deserves scrutiny
description: Anthropic’s AI constitution bakes in enough ambiguity over the ‘personhood’ of AI for bots to claim rights someday—which may come to prove perilous for humanity. While the AI company’s approach may be well-motivated, it needs a rethink.

title: How has Indian consumption performed this year? Impressively, though mixed signals persist
description: Signs of a pickup in 2026-27 exist with some contrasting signals. The broad outlook seems brighter. After a long wait, can we finally expect both consumption and investment to fire together as the economy’s two big growth engines?

title: Is there a case for raising India's inflation target? There’s clearly some scope for a discussion on it
description: How inflation is behaving elsewhere matters when deciding the country's inflation target. Global price instability makes space for a debate over the ideal rate for monetary policymakers to pursue. But no change can be made in haste.

title: Follow the buzz? A headlong rush for data centres in India may cost the country dear
description: Artificial intelligence (AI) has led them to proliferate. Given their long-term effects and uncertain benefits, however, we should weigh various factors carefully before joining the global rush. Why would anyone think they’re best placed in orbit?

title: Mint Quick Edit | India’s exports to Brics trade partners have risen rapidly: retain the momentum
description: With world trade rattled by geopolitics, India’s push to diversify its export markets has gotten a Brics boost. This is heartening. Can it also help achieve a better balance of imports and exports with China?

title: Tata Sons at the crossroads: who guards the institution?
description: The reappointment of Chandrasekaran as Tata Sons chairman raises critical questions about governance, ownership, and regulatory oversight. The RBI’s recent decisions add complexity. So, who should lead Tata Sons? What should Tata Sons evolve into?

title: Demographic U-turn: Indian states are reversing their population policies—will they succeed?
description: Countries around the world are adopting anti-Malthusian policies to encourage citizens to have more children. Indian states have pro-natalist schemes too. However, workplace backups like good infant care and parental leave may work better than ‘baby bonuses.'

title: India’s China dilemma is about capability, not import reduction
description: India should judge de-risking not by whether imports from China decline, but by whether dependence is converted into domestic capability and greater strategic choice.

title: AI oversight: The UK has already built the watchdog that America’s tech royalty say they want
description: Leaders of artificial intelligence (AI) firms in the US say they would like a supervisory system for this technology, while the Trump administration has been unsure. London’s AI Security Institute is perfectly placed to evaluate risks. Here's why.

title: Personal guarantee muddle: no insolvency process can manufacture asset value that doesn't exist
description: The Subhash Chandra personal-guarantee case under India’s Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) reminds us of the need to make fine distinctions that too many observers miss. For instance, an insolvency process cannot distribute what a guarantor’s estate does not contain.

title: The Tata model is one of India's unique contributions to capitalism—it mustn’t get undone
description: Minority shareholders have rights, the Reserve Bank of India has responsibilities and governance rules must be respected. But a compromise path must be found that does not sacrifice the Tata inheritance. A societal asset mustn't suffer collateral damage in a boardroom or regulatory conflict.

title: What becomes of the Tata way
description: The battle over N. Chandrasekaran’s reappointment and Tata Sons’ listing has exposed a deeper question: who safeguards the values and purpose of the Tata Group when its institutions disagree?

title: Connecting India’s youth to global markets could vastly improve rural livelihoods—here's how
description: The Brics declaration has opened up a large labour rewarding opportunity for the country. To leverage this, India needs programmes to impart skills that enable the export of labour and help rural producers access overseas markets.

title: War over Tata Sons: The business principle of owner’s agency cannot be overlooked
description: The case for Tata Sons’ public issue is pitched on group transparency as a public good. However, going about it via a board resolution that treads a legal grey zone would be problematic. Tata Trusts own Tata Sons. Ends matter—but so do means.

title: Mint Quick Edit | Tata turbulence: why Venu Srinivasan’s role is in India’s spotlight
description: The TVS industrialist who flipped his stance on Tata Sons’ listing has played a pivotal part in the drama unfolding at Bombay House over the holding company’s future. No wonder his role as a Tata Trust trustee and Tata Sons director is abuzz with questions.

title: Are we seeing the return of an age of bloody wars?
description: It’s clear the days of bloody wars have returned. Exhausted by two world wars, humanity created institutions like the United Nations. However, today the hallowed institution presents a sad picture of its growing irrelevance.

title: Urban heroism: city authorities should take note of public support for officials who do their jobs right
description: Patience with shoddy public services in Indian cities is wearing thin. Urban India’s frustrations can be gauged from the adulation reserved for public officials who are dedicated to their jobs with due sincerity and diligence.

title: Mint Explainer | What potential commission caps could mean for insurers
description: Irdai could set different commission ceilings for individual agents, agencies and bank-led distribution, while shifting compensation away from large upfront payouts.

title: Axis Max Life sees no immediate trigger for premium hikes, bets on small towns
description: Axis Max Life CEO Sumit Madan says India's insurance industry is having a “reasonably good run” despite global uncertainties.

title: Mint Explainer | Public insurance registry: how Irdai wants to build a digital backbone for insurance
description: Irdai's proposed registry could link policy, claims and risk data across insurers while connecting insurance with lenders, identity systems and public databases.

title: Insurance agents, brokers may get lower commission after GST cuts
description: Following the GST cut on insurance policies, insurers may reduce commissions for intermediaries to manage increased costs. With competitive pressures and regulatory caps, companies are seeking digital partnerships and expense rationalization to sustain growth while passing benefits to customers.

title: Bima Sugam India Federation website launch: IRDAI Chairman says ‘milestone’ for insurance sector — all you need to know
description: IRDAI has launched Bima Sugam, a digital platform aimed at creating a comprehensive Digital Public Infrastructure for insurance, promoting transparency and empowering policyholders. Here's all you need to know.

title: Why insurance sector is E-commerce firms' favourite poaching ground
description: Well-trained salesmen, with strong customer relations make the insurance sector prime target for e-commerce industry. They are wooing insurance workers with attractive bonuses, and flexible working hours.

title: Netizen says  ₹61 lakh cashless claim for  ₹2.40 crore policy rejected, Niva Bupa denies ‘baseless allegation’
description: A post has alleged that Niva Bupa denied  ₹61 lakh cashless claim for a cancer patient, despite a  ₹2.40 crore policy, while the company has denied the accusation, saying the pre-approved  ₹25 lakh is available to the family.&nbsp;

title: GST 2.0: Health insurance firms may raise policy tariffs by 3-5% to compensate for input tax credit losses amid tax cuts
description: GST 2.0: Health insurance firms may raise policy tariffs by 3-5% to offset their losses incurred from the input tax credit. Here's what industry experts think of this potential move, and how risky it is for the insurance sector.&nbsp;

title: GST rate cut on insurance: Should you wait till September 22 to buy new policy? Experts weigh in
description: As the central government cuts GST on individual life insurance policies from 18 per cent to nil, policyholders — new and old — are likely to benefit from September 22. Here's all you need to know.
